6. Mr. Nirmalendu Deb, learned advocate for the accused petitioner submits that the case is barred by limitation inasmuch as it is apparent from the petition of complaint that the complainant issued 1st notice under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act on 12.08.2012 through courier service and served another legal notice with registered A/D on 23.08.2012. He submits that under Section 138 (b) of the Negotiable Instrument Act one notice would be served and cause of action arose from the date of receipt of that notice. But in the petition of complaint, it is not mentioned when the accused petitioner received the notice. According to Mr. Deb, cause of action arose from the date of receipt of first notice dated 12.08.2012 but no date is mentioned in the petition of complaint relating to receipt of the notice by the accused petitioner and thus failure to mention any legal cause of action in the petition of complaint rendered the case liable to be quashed. In support of his contention, learned Advocate referred the case of Nizamuddin Mahmood vs. Abdul Hamid Bhuiyan and another, reported in 9 MLR (AD) 299. Mr. Nirmalendu Dev also submits that if the allegation made in the petition of complaint is taken as true then also the same does not create any offence inasmuch as the complainant and the accused petitioner are step brother and sister, through one father and two mother, and as such the allegation of the petition of complaint are preposterous, absurd and improbable. He also submits that the complainant opened the account in the name of his sister, the accused petitioner, when her age was only 17 years 9 months and 9 days and at that time the accused petitioner only passed her secondary school certificate examination, who at present is a student of Honor's class. He submits that the accused petitioner was neither a service holder nor engaged in any business and as such the story of loan amount of taka 10 lacs as stated in the petition of complaint is preposterous and improbable. Mr. Dev next submits that the complainant fraudulently filed the petition of complaint with a criminal intention to doom life of his step sister, the accused petitioner. He further submits that it is settled principle of law that fraud vitiates everything. 

 9. It appears from the petition of complaint annexed with the application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure that a cheque was issued by the accused petitioner in favour of the complaint-opposite party no.1 on 28.02.2012 and within six months the complaint opposite party no.1 presented the cheque in his Bank account for encashment on different dates lastly on 08.08.2012, but each and every time, the cheque was dishonored by the Bank for "insufficient fund". Thereafter, the complainant served legal notice on 12.08.2012 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. through courier service which was received by the accused petitioner but she did not take any step for payment of the loan amount, then the complainant served another legal notice on 28.3.2012 with registered A/D. Thereafter, the complainant filed the petition of complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act within time as prescribed by the law. The 1st  point raised by Mr. Deb that the petition of complaint is barred by limitation is not tenable in the eye of law inasmuch as it is apparent that the complainant filed the petition of complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sylhet, on 07.10.2012 i.e. within 60 days from the date of 1st notice.
